title: WHAT THE DATA SAY: Half of Americans would rather do ‘kidulting’ than talk to a therapist, drink or go to a party
body_markdown:
By: Ray Day


## **CONTACT:**


Ray Day
ray.day@stagwellglobal.com


*We wanted to share our latest consumer and business insights, based on research from[Stagwell](https://www.stagwellglobal.com/) and[Allison Worldwide](https://www.allisonworldwide.com/) .* *Among the highlights of our weekly* *consumer sentiment tracking:*


**PLAYTIME ISN’T JUST FOR KIDS**


Adults are embracing “kidulting” – from collectibles and crafts to immersive experiences – as a new source of connection and self-care, according to[The Rise of Kidulting Report](https://san.com/wp-content/uploads/securepdfs/2026/10/Kidulting-Poll.pdf) from The Harris Poll.


- 80% of Americans and 94% of Gen Z participated in playful activities for their own enjoyment in the past year.
- Play is increasingly a coping mechanism, as 83% say small moments of joy feel important in uncertain times, while 75% say playful hobbies help build emotional resilience.
- 51% of Americans would rather do “kidulting” activities than talk to a therapist, 49% would choose them over drinks and 47% over going to a party.
- 40% call playful products and experiences a creative outlet, 40% say they bring more joy to daily life, and 30% see them as self-care.
- 65% of Americans spent at least $100 on a playful product or activity in the past year, rising to 80% of Gen Z and 78% of Millennials.
- 62% want more adult-only nights at theme parks, museums or zoos, while 60% want nostalgic movie or cartoon marathons in theaters or bars.
- 77% say brands underestimate adults’ appetite for playfully designed experiences, and 67% are actively seeking brands, products and experiences that make life feel lighter.
- *See also:*[Millennials are ‘kidulting’ through their parenthood stage, spending their free time on blind boxes and claw machines](https://fortune.com/2026/10/20/millennials-kidulting-harris-poll-nostalgia-blind-box-arcade-claw/)


**AI IS HOLIDAY SHOPPERS’ HELPER**


Consumers are ready to bring AI into holiday shopping – from finding deals and discovering brands to making purchases, based on new Harris Poll research with[Forter.](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/two-thirds-of-us-consumers-plan-to-shop-with-ai-this-holiday-season-new-forter-research-finds-302913539.html)


- 67% of U.S. consumers plan to use AI for holiday shopping this year.
- More than one-third of holiday shoppers (37%) expect to use AI more than they did last year.
- Adoption is especially strong among younger shoppers: 83% of adults ages 18–34 plan to use AI for holiday shopping, compared with 40% of those age 65 and older.
- 43% of Americans have discovered or bought from a new retailer because of an AI recommendation. This goes up to 68% among younger adults.
- 78% of holiday shoppers are comfortable letting AI handle at least one aspect of their shopping journey, and more than half (53%) would be comfortable allowing AI to autonomously purchase a holiday gift, depending on the cost.


**CREDIT RELIANCE CONTINUES**


Americans are feeling more in control of their finances – yet many, especially parents and younger adults, are leaning on credit to make ends meet, based on Harris Poll data and NerdWallet’s[October Consumer Financial Resilience Index](https://www.nerdwallet.com/finance/studies/financial-resilience-index) .


- 78% of Americans say they feel in control of their day-to-day finances, up from 73% in September.
- 38% expect to rely on credit for at least some expenses this month.
- Parents are under pressure, as 54% of parents with children under 18 expect to use credit, up from 44% the prior month and well above the 30% of non-parents who say the same.
- More than half of Gen Z (53%) and Millennials (51%) anticipate relying on credit, compared with 37% of Gen X and 17% of Boomers.
- Two-thirds of Americans (67%) say they could cover an unexpected $1,000 expense with cash. Yet that drops to 39% among households earning less than $50,000.
- Men (84%) are more likely than women (74%) to feel in control of their finances and to have a $1,000 emergency cash buffer (71% men versus 63% women).
- 65% of Americans expect the U.S. economy to enter a recession within the next 12 months.
- *See also:[New survey reveals how chronic stress impacts U.S. adults](https://www.news-medical.net/news/20261022/New-survey-reveals-how-chronic-stress-impacts-US-adults.aspx)*


**THE ENTREPRENEUR EFFECT**


Entrepreneurs are finding success and wishing they had started sooner by building businesses around a focused idea, according to research from Harris Poll and[Shopify](https://cdn.shopify.com/static/the-entrepreneur-effect/the-entrepreneur-effect-report.pdf) .


- 95% of entrepreneurs say building their company is among their proudest accomplishments.
- More than half (57%) of entrepreneurs wish they had started sooner.
- 86% of entrepreneurs say e-commerce platforms have made starting a business easier than it was a decade ago.
- Two in five businesses (41%) on Shopify launched with just a single product.
- *See also:[Some hiring managers may be waiting until after the election to recruit](https://www.hrdive.com/news/hiring-managers-waiting-until-after-the-election-to-recruit/833566/)*
